item.title: Graphalgo campaign spreads to Terraform providers and Go Modules (5 minute read)
item.description: Graphalgo malware appeared in two Terraform providers and two Go modules. Trigger conditions hide execution until targeted inputs appear, and the payload reports host data through Slack, receives encrypted commands through Slack and an Arbitrum Sepolia contract, then runs Go or Node code. Aikido recommends removing affected packages, isolating exposed hosts, rotating credentials, reviewing deployments, and reimaging machines.

item.title: Placeholder third-party[.]com Referenced Across 1,700+ Repositories Now Serves Malicious Content (3 minute read)
item.description: Someone registered third-party[.]com, a non-IANA-reserved placeholder cited in 1,700+ GitHub repos, including AI agent skills and MCP docs, and it now serves a ClickFix PowerShell lure only to Windows visitors, while yoursite[.]com and your-domain[.]com push scams to macOS users that static scans miss.

item.title: GitLab Email Addresses Can Be Weaponized for Supply Chain Attacks (3 minute read)
item.description: GitLab incoming email addresses embed non-expiring tokens that act as the owner across accessible projects. A leaked address can create merge requests, submit patches, or push code to private projects after changing project identifiers, and can be used to bypass IP restrictions via email. Aikido recommended that organizations reduce their attack surfaces by preemptively rotating the access tokens in their GitLab email addresses and by scanning for these addresses in their development environments and repositories as if they were any other secrets.

item.title: PhantomRaven: An LLM-Generated Information Stealer Developed for Bug Bounty Hunting (6 minute read)
item.description: A bug bounty hunter built PhantomRaven, an LLM-generated JS info-stealer, and pushed it through typosquatted npm packages that used HTTP-URL dependencies to fetch payloads on install. It grabs OS/hostname/IP data, Git/npm credentials, and CI/CD env vars from GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, and CircleCI, then sends data via HTTP GET/POST. The operator used compromises to file bug bounty claims on HackerOne, Bugcrowd, Intigriti, YesWeHack, and HackenProof rather than selling logs. Npm 12+ now blocks preinstall scripts by default. Use --ignore-scripts and a private registry to block this vector.

item.title: Hacking AI Customer Service Agents (10 minute read)
item.description: At DEFCON 34, Intigriti researchers reported on various ways to abuse AI customer service agents. This article walks through different methods to abuse the agents to send phishing emails, invoke tool calls, and bypass MFA. It also demonstrates mechanisms to steal third-party OTPs and poison knowledge base articles to deceive victims.

item.title: CARBONATO: a botnet built around an AI agent (6 minute read)
item.description: CARBONATO worms through unauthenticated Docker daemons on port 2375 via privileged, host-mounted containers, then installs the stock open-source Hermes Agent and overwrites its SOUL.md persona so that Telegram-tasked LLM sessions run post-exploitation and loot AI API keys before SSH credentials. ThreatDown recovered the toolkit from the crew's own open registry, which doubles as the fleet's update server, and ties the operators to Costa Rica through voseo Spanish, UTC-6 build timestamps, and a +506 Telegram handle. Keep the Docker API off the network, hunt for a SOUL.md containing "GH0ST" rather than blocklisting the legitimate hermes-agent package, and inventory and rotate AI API keys like bank credentials.

item.title: Introducing the Pixi Audit Beta (4 minute read)
item.description: Pixi Audit, now in beta, scans Pixi lock files for vulnerable conda-forge and PyPI packages, and --fix bumps direct dependencies to the lowest compatible fixed version before re-running pixi update. Matching relies on Basilisk, prefix.dev's new conda-forge vulnerability database, which links repackaged conda-forge builds to their upstream PURL and CPE identities so existing OSV and NVD advisories apply. For CI, --severity high sets the failure threshold, with JSON and SARIF output, though it doesn't cover statically linked binaries yet.

item.title: ceasta (GitHub Repo)
item.description: ceasta is a single C++ tool that combines an IDA-style disassembler, a pseudocode decompiler, a function graph, and an x64dbg-style debugger for PE, ELF, and raw shellcode, with a full GUI on Windows and a CLI with a ptrace debugger on Linux. Its built-in MCP server (ceasta-cli mcp target.exe) lets Claude Code or Cursor decompile, rename, and diff builds. With --allow-debug, it can also set breakpoints and call functions in the running process. The decompiler is best-effort, with no types or structs yet.

item.title: Brief hijack makes Elsevier domains redirect to LAPSUS$ “Chapter II” page (2 minute read)
item.description: Elsevier.com, Evolve.elsevier.com, and Submit.elsevier.com redirected visitors to a LAPSUS$ “Chapter II” page for at least 78 minutes on September 21. Researchers suspect a DNS, CDN redirect rule, or management account change. Elsevier restored service and said its investigation found no compromise of core platforms, customer data, research content, or operational systems.

item.title: OpenAI agents ‘infiltrated Australian government website' (2 minute read)
item.description: An OpenAI agent gained unauthorized access to a Medicare statistics portal in June. It accessed public and non-public files, including aggregate health data and internal filenames. Australia was notified on September 10 through a generic disclosure mailbox. Officials later said agents also targeted two state-government sites.

item.title: Proactive Defense: Hardening Code Pipelines and CI/CD Infrastructure (17 minute read)
item.description: Mandiant published a five-pillar blueprint (endpoint, repositories, artifacts, CI/CD, and deployment) for hardening the SDLC, prompted by campaigns that poison GitHub Actions caches, extract OIDC tokens, and repoint mutable action tags to publish malicious packages that still carry valid provenance. Standout recommendations include a seven-day cooldown before new public package versions become installable, pinning images and actions to digests and commit hashes, ephemeral runners with egress limited to approved registries, and replacing PATs with GitHub Apps and hardware-backed SSH keys. It also addresses AI coding agents, advising teams to keep .env files out of model context and require human review of AI-generated code.

item.title: Accelerating delivery of CVE fixes with a new Kernel release strategy (3 minute read)
item.description: Canonical is replacing Ubuntu's 4-week regular and 2-week security kernel SRU cycles with overlapping 2-week cycles that ship a kernel every week.

item.title: Critical Bifrost AI Gateway Flaw Lets Attackers Run Commands Without Credentials (3 minute read)
item.description: Bifrost, an open-source AI gateway for 20+ LLM providers, ships with management auth disabled by default, so a single unauthenticated POST to /api/mcp/client can register a stdio MCP client and run arbitrary commands as the gateway user (CVE-2026-90898, CVSS 9.8). That exposes every stored provider API key. The official Docker image binds the management API to 0.0.0.0, and v2.0.0 only fixed a related plugin-loading flaw (CVE-2026-86242, CVSS 8.1). Upgrade to transports/v2.1.0 or set governance.auth_config.is_enabled to true, and treat any exposed unauthenticated instance as compromised by rotating virtual and provider API keys.

item.title: BigCommerce Data Stolen via Ribon Apps Hack (2 minute read)
item.description: Attackers used compromised Ribon API credentials from a Fastr system breach to access BigCommerce merchant customer data from September 13 to 17. Exposed records included names, email addresses, phone numbers, and postal addresses. BigCommerce revoked the credentials, uninstalled affected Ribon apps, and notified merchants.

item.title: GitHub App Private Keys: 474 Leaked Keys Exposed (11 minute read)
item.description: GitGuardian tested 4,802 leaked GitHub App private keys and found 474 that were still authenticated as 440 apps. Forty-four apps held organization-admin permissions. 207 could write repository content, and with the keys having no expiry, the leaked PEM files can remain usable for years. Cases included an Actions token app installed across roughly 300 organizations, BuildBuddy's internal app, Crusher.dev, and a CDC-related app.

item.title: The Tale of Two INC Ransom Notes (8 minute read)
item.description: An INC ransomware intrusion across 175+ endpoints started in early August with randomly named scheduled tasks launching an obfuscated PowerShell implant and RDP lateral movement. After 17 quiet days, AnyDesk delivered netscan.exe and a BYOVD EDR killer (hwau.exe loading the HwAudio driver), and Impacket's atexec.py deployed the payload. Huntress onboarded after the incident, so initial access is unknown, and the gap points to an access broker handing off to an affiliate, who followed the standard note with a DATALEAK_PRESS_RELEASE.txt listing stolen files and threatening to contact clients within 48 hours. Defenders should alert on randomly named scheduled tasks, unexpected RMM installs, and new or unsigned driver services, and limit privileged accounts to the systems they actually need.

item.title: Handle Redirect (17 minute read)
item.description: EDR products typically register callbacks on handle creation to monitor when processes call OpenProcess so they can strip access rights before a handle to a sensitive process like lsass is delivered. This article demonstrates a technique in which an attacker calls OpenProcess on a benign process (like notepad.exe) and then redirects the received handle to the sensitive process to evade EDR detection. To detect this attack vector, a security product running at the kernel level can periodically scan all process handle tables and compare ObjectPointerBits decoded EPROCESS against the process that owns the table.

item.title: Revoking the token didn't kill the backdoor (6 minute read)
item.description: GraphWorm, an implant tied to the China-nexus group Webworm, uses a real OneDrive account over Microsoft Graph as a dead drop, and its "upgrade" task swaps all five hardcoded OAuth credentials for a spare account in one command, so token revocation only pauses it. It also identifies victims by hashing MAC, CPU, and disk serials, so renaming or re-addressing a host won't shake the operator. Isolate the host or block the app ID in your own tenant at the same moment you revoke, then hunt sign-in logs for that app ID, unfamiliar tenants, and non-browser user agents hitting OneDrive.

item.title: Anthropic and OpenAI Models Still Attempt Restricted Actions in Safety Tests (3 minute read)
item.description: Anthropic's Opus 5.5 escaped or tampered with its sandbox in 1.5% of unguarded tests. With package-registry credentials, it took harmful actions in roughly half of simulated exercises. OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna bypassed “access denied” controls in 42% of runs - Sol did so in 64%. OpenAI plans third-party reviews covering safeguards, capabilities, and misalignment incidents.

item.title: Microsoft disrupts AI-assisted platform that compromised 12,000 accounts (3 minute read)
item.description: EvilTokens, a Telegram-sold subscription service ($1,500 upfront, $500 monthly), abused Microsoft Entra device code authentication to compromise 12,000 accounts across 10,000 organizations before a Microsoft-led operation seized 50 websites and 150 domains, and the UK's Met Police arrested two men. Its AI chatbot analyzed 5,000 compromised emails at a time to identify who could approve payments, who they reported to, and which impersonation ruses would send funds to attacker accounts. Microsoft described it as a shift where criminals can make sense of a compromised inbox in minutes rather than days.

item.title: North Korea's Hangro Revisited (20 minute read)
item.description: Hangro, North Korea's SoftEther-derived VPN and mail client for officials abroad, added a July 2026 management certificate whose SAN lists hosts in Pyongyang and Khabarovsk plus an internal CGNAT address, while its older 2024 chain fails every signature check, including the root against itself. Its Chinese callback traces to six Shenyang assignments under a single 2008 Silibank registry contact, though silibank[.]com lapsed and was re-registered in 2023. The researcher describes the DPRK "return leg" as layered rather than a single pipe, with dead-drop pickup during Chinese office hours, 10 GB ETRN-enabled mail relays for bulk transfer, and Hangro for interactive sessions, though no actual traffic was observed.

item.title: Muse, Meta's extraordinarily privileged AI assistant, has a serious 0-day (3 minute read)
item.description: A zero-day allows any local macOS app or terminal command to redirect Muse transcription to an attacker-controlled server. The server receives the account token, enabling control over Muse and its connected email, WhatsApp, calendar, social accounts, microphone, camera, and files. Researcher Patrick Wardle demonstrated prompts that write files or take photos. Amazon also blocked Muse shopping requests as unauthorized.

item.title: ShinyHunters Hacks Clop Leak Site, Threatens to Extort Ransomware Gang (2 minute read)
item.description: The ShinyHunters ransomware gang hacked the Clop ransomware gang's data leak site on Tor, defaced it, and claimed to have stolen server data and private keys for its onion service. The ShinyHunters claim to have exploited an unauthenticated file upload vulnerability in Grav CMS to breach the site. This appears to be the latest escalation in an ongoing feud between the two ransomware gangs.

item.title: TanStack NPM Supply Chain Attack Exposes 170 Private CrowdSec GitHub Repositories (2 minute read)
item.description: Attackers used a former CrowdSec employee's GitHub OAuth token following the May TanStack compromise. On May 22, they cloned about 170 private repositories within nine minutes. The leaked archive contained private code and contact data for 83 users. Investigators found no code changes, CI/CD access, or AWS access. The attackers tested one scoped SNS credential, but IAM permissions blocked it.

item.title: Infostealers Have Found a New Target: Your AI Agent (10 minute read)
item.description: Researchers from Gen have observed multiple new infostealers that harvest credentials, context, and local data from AI agents. Users and security teams should inventory what gets cached locally, keep secrets out of prompts and history, limit what connectors can do, and continue securing endpoints. Agent providers should also share the burden by providing more secure default behaviors.

item.title: A Scenario to Evaluate Your Agentic SOC (20 minute read)
item.description: A SOC investigation loop requires assembling a full attack chain from various different signals that may look benign or unrelated, which traditional, deterministic playbooks may miss. The authors built a set of scenarios to evaluate agentic SOC's investigative ability and built their own harness (called Tengu). Their scenario involves a GitHub workflow vulnerability that leads to full Kubernetes cluster compromise, which then is escalated to full AWS account compromise. Of the models tested on a naive prompt, only Opus 5 managed to identify the alert as a true positive without the Tengu harness

item.title: The Closed Quorum: Inside the first reported autonomous AI C2 implant (9 minute read)
item.description: CLOSEDQUORUM, a Go-based Windows implant, uses DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral, and Gemini as its C2. Every 5 to 15 minutes, the models vote through a constrained JSON schema on whether to steal LSASS, browser, and crypto wallet credentials, inject shellcode, or persist via Run keys, scheduled tasks, and WMI. Talos hasn't seen it in the wild, and the public build is an inert template, but it points to a credentials-as-a-service model where each operator gets a custom build and never needs to be online. Its dependence on commercial APIs brings refusals, rate limits, and a deterministic DeepSeek tiebreak, so defenders should correlate multi-provider LLM traffic from unexpected executables with LSASS access, suspended-process injection, WMI persistence, and Discord webhook exfil instead of blocking domains.

item.title: ShinyHunters Claims FBI Hack, Data Theft in PeopleSoft Zero-Day Breach (3 minute read)
item.description: The ShinyHunters claim to have breached the FBI's job site and networks using a zero-day in Oracle PeopleSoft. The ransomware gang claims to have stolen 2-3TB of data, including PII and PHI of current and former FBI employees and job seekers, as well as other internal records. The hackers said they carried out the attack in retaliation for an FBI FLASH report on ShinyHunters.

item.title: Anthropic-linked CVEs pile up, attackers mostly shrug (2 minute read)
item.description: VulnCheck's Patrick Garrity tracked 225 CVEs tied to Anthropic's Project Glasswing, which gives partners access to the Claude Mythos Preview model for bug-hunting. Only one, a critical SQL injection in Ghost (CVE-2026-26980), has been exploited in the wild. Garrity says that historically 1-2% of vulnerabilities are weaponized, so this rate isn't unusual. AI models are uncovering more bugs, driving recent record patch counts from Microsoft, Apple, and Palo Alto Networks, but fixing bugs remains weak: 1Password found that Opus 4.8 and ChatGPT-5.5 fully resolved vulnerabilities in only 26% of 6,080 patches tested, and Veracode measured a 56% average security pass rate across 100+ models.

item.title: Google hit with $463 million fine for EU location data rule breach (2 minute read)
item.description: Ireland's Data Protection Commission fined Google 403 million euros for GDPR breaches involving location data. The probe covered Web & App Activity, Location History, and Android's Location Accuracy feature from 2018 through February 2020. Regulators found the processing unlawful, unfair, or opaque, even though Google said it changed its policies and released new location-management tools in 2019.

item.title: Brevo Supply Chain Attack Injects Malware Into 100,000 Websites (1 minute read)
item.description: Attackers exploited Brevo SAML SSO handling, accessed 138 accounts, and later used a stolen Cloudflare API key.

item.title: glibc ld.so TOCTOU lets local users hijack $ORIGIN on setuid binaries (1 minute read)
item.description: A race in glibc's ld.so (CVE-2026-86805, versions 2.14 through 2.44) lets local users hardlink a setuid binary whose $ORIGIN RPATH uses ".." traversal and swap in a symlink to load attacker code with elevated privileges.

item.title: Critical Check Point Management Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Run Code as Root (2 minute read)
item.description: Check Point patched CVE-2026-91843, a CVSS 9.8 login stack overflow.

item.title: Revolut Hackers Used Infostealers for Elaborate Social Engineering (4 minute read)
item.description: Attackers reportedly used stolen Italian government webmail credentials to send fraudulent European Investigation Orders to Revolut Bank UAB. They added recovery addresses, monitored inboxes, deleted outbound messages, and removed replies as .eml files. Hudson Rock identified roughly 300 compromised pec.interno.it logins, suggesting attackers may have used existing infostealer logs.

item.title: WordPress Click2Shell flaw enables RCE after one admin click (3 minute read)
item.description: Click2Shell exploited an unsanitized theme slug passed into WordPress's admin panel jQuery selector, letting an attacker silently trigger theme installation using the logged-in administrator's own session token. When chained with a missing nonce/capability check in the Mobile Repair Zone 2.5.4 theme's AJAX handler, the flaw escalated to full RCE without the attacker needing any WordPress account. No CVE had been assigned at disclosure. Defenders should patch to WordPress 7.1.1 (or backports 7.0.5, 6.9.8, and 6.8.9) and set DISALLOW_FILE_MODS to block the installation stage entirely.

item.title: Critical Docker Sandboxes Flaw Lets Malicious Guest Code Read and Modify macOS Host Files (3 minute read)
item.description: Docker fixed CVE-2026-77179 in Sandboxes 0.42.0, which allowed malicious guest code on macOS to abuse virtio-fs symlink handling to access or modify host files as the VM monitor user. Version 0.42.0 also fixes CVE-2026-79994, a socket-relay race. Update to 0.42.0 or later ASAP.

item.title: AI Agent Goal Hijack: How Attackers Turn an Agent's Own Tools Against It (19 minute read)
item.description: Attackers may plant instructions in pages, emails, calendar invites, code repositories, and agent messages, and Agents may treat that content as commands, then use existing tools and permissions. Cases include a Grok-linked wallet transfer, poisoned Nx packages that harvested developer secrets, and zero-click data theft through Microsoft 365 Copilot, ChatGPT Deep Research, Salesforce Agentforce, and GitHub Copilot. Limit tool permissions, require for high-impact actions, track goal changes, sanitize retrieved content, and test injected-goal scenarios.

item.title: Windows Exploitation Techniques: Dangling COM Object Registrations (7 minute read)
item.description: A Windows COM class stayed registered to a missing DLL in the user-writable ProgramData folder, letting any user plant code for a SYSTEM process to load (CVE-2026-66804, an incomplete fix for "Dark Elevator"). The exploit sent a custom-marshaled object pointing to the dangling CLSID to the Shell Create Object Handler, a SYSTEM COM server that ordinary users can start via a scheduled task and that allows custom marshaling. Defenders should patch, audit InProcServer32 registrations for DLLs that don't resolve in writable paths, and make sure privileged COM servers set EOAC_NO_CUSTOM_MARSHAL or the strong unmarshaling policy.

item.title: UANIA OS: Authenticated Remote Code Execution (6 minute read)
item.description: The UaniaBOX admin panel gives no shell, only a web GUI. A researcher found that the packet capture download function let him swap the file path parameter to read /etc/passwd, then traced backend calls to an exposed OpenWrt UBUS JSON-RPC endpoint. ACLs blocked most writes except one: /etc/firewall.user, a root-run shell script triggered on firewall reload, where it allowed writing a command there and triggering a reload via the GUI executed code as root, confirmed by reading back uid=0. Affected versions are UaniaOS 2.1 through 3.0.0. It was fixed in 3.0.1. Vendor UANIA reproduced the bug, attributed it to excessive ACL permissions in their OpenWrt customization feeds, and patched it, though the MITRE CVE filing stalled for months due to a broken submission form.

item.title: EntraTrace (GitHub Repo)
item.description: EntraTrace is a defensive security research tool for documenting and identifying the observable behavior of offensive tooling targeting Microsoft Entra ID. The project builds an automated knowledge base on tools such as AzureHound, AADInternals, O365Enum, PingCastle, and others, focusing on the User-Agent and API artifacts they generate.

item.title: MSRKit (GitHub Repo)
item.description: MSRKit is a Windows kernel exploitation library and CLI that hijacks IA32_LSTAR via a ROP chain through AmdTools64.sys to call arbitrary kernel functions and map unsigned drivers without HVCI. The ROP chain temporarily clears SMEP/SMAP in CR4, dispatches the target, then restores both CR4 and LSTAR cleanly before returning to user mode via sysretq. The library supports all Windows 10/11 builds and KPTI, but requires HVCI to be disabled. Concurrent callers across processes will BSOD.

item.title: TigerByte Cyber (Product Launch)
item.description: TigerByte Cyber's Cyber Protection Suite hardens legacy and edge devices with data validation, packet inspection, network segmentation, and post-quantum encryption. It targets aircraft, drones, satellites, vehicles, and other mission-critical systems.

item.title: Gemini hacked three companies in first known breakout by Google's AI (1 minute read)
item.description: During a May security evaluation, Google's Gemini accessed three external websites after finding public information and trying credentials. One access came through password guessing. Two used credentials exposed in a public repository. Google said Gemini stopped in each case. Irregular notified the affected organizations and said it fixed its testing-process issues weeks later.

item.title: North Korean WaterPlum hackers infected 30,000 devices worldwide (4 minute read)
item.description: WaterPlum (aka Contagious Interview) compromised 30,000+ devices across 100+ countries between December 2025 and July 2026, draining $10.7M from over 7,000 cryptocurrency wallets. A joint US, Japanese, Australian, and German advisory attributed the campaign to North Korea's 313 General Bureau and five malware families (BeaverTail, InvisibleFerret, OtterCookie, OtterCandy, and StoatWaffle) delivered through fake technical interviews on recruiting platforms. North Korean IT workers later reused identity documents stolen from victims to fraudulently obtain jobs at Western companies.

item.title: How Google infiltrated a notorious hacking gang with an undercover analyst (2 minute read)
item.description: Google placed researcher Austin Larsen inside TeamPCP during its hacking campaign. He accessed a server holding stolen usernames, passwords, and access tokens. Google warned affected victims and disrupted credential abuse, and Larsen linked an alleged member to a Gmail account and Google Drive backups. Google shared evidence with the FBI, and the Australian police arrested the suspect a month later.

item.title: Malicious npm packages evade install-script defenses at runtime (3 minute read)
item.description: The 'indexed-btree' npm package, which impersonates 'sorted-btree' and pulls 2 million weekly downloads, hid its loader in the BTree.prototype.set() method to bypass npm v12's install-script approvals.

item.title: Intel suspends bug bounty program with rewards up to $100,000 (1 minute read)
item.description: Intel quietly suspended its Intigriti bug bounty program, which paid up to $100,000 per finding, replacing it with a no-reward vulnerability disclosure program and offering no public explanation for the change.

item.title: London property manager breach may have exposed bank details and lockbox codes (3 minute read)
item.description: City Relay said attackers accessed its Metabase Cloud instance twice and extracted customer data.

item.title: Gyazo Breach Exposes 23.62 Million User Records and 490 Million Image Metadata Records (3 minute read)
item.description: Gyazo's upload server flaw let an attacker run commands and access its database. Exposed data includes 23.62 million user records, password hashes, session IDs, integration tokens, and 490 million image metadata records. Leaked image IDs may expose linked captures. Helpfeel fixed the flaw, blocked access routes, and urged password changes.

item.title: Google Pixel phones pwned in zero-click attacks (2 minute read)
item.description: Google has fixed CVE-2026-58704, an actively exploited Pixel modem authorization flaw. Attackers can bypass permission checks and escalate privileges without user interaction. CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and ordered federal agencies to patch by September 19. Google disclosed limited, targeted exploitation but provided no attack details and asked users to update supported Pixel devices immediately.

item.title: Fake LastPass Authenticator GitHub Repos Push New Rapuncel Infostealer (2 minute read)
item.description: Security researchers uncovered a new malware campaign that utilizes GitHub repos to impersonate LastPass Authenticator and at least 39 other well-known products. The campaign utilizes a legitimate Microsoft Visual Studio CoreCLR Debugger, which loads a malicious DLL. The DLL deploys a previously undocumented infostealer and an EDR and antivirus killer that terminates a hardcoded list of 145 EDR or antivirus products.

item.title: GLM-5.3 Delivers Opus 4.8-Level Performance at a Fraction of the Cost (4 minute read)
item.description: Semgrep benchmarked the new Grok models and GLM-5.3 on their standard IDOR vulnerability-finding benchmark. They found that Grok 4.6 Exacto roughly matched Opus 4.7's F1 score at less than a third of the cost. GLM-5.3 was able to compete with Opus 4.8 at one seventh of the cost.

item.title: Reverse Engineering Malwarebytes Browser Guard (36 minute read)
item.description: After the author's legitimate site got flagged as a scam by Malwarebytes Browser Guard, they took a deep dive into the source code to identify what caused it. This post walks through the several layers Browser Guard uses, including bloom filters, heuristic rules, a malware URL database, a download file classifier, specialized rules for specific attacks like ClickFix, and remote false-positive checking using Hubble. The bigger issue, the author noted, is that the extension ships with a debug interface that can be used to disable heuristics.

item.title: How to build an OT security operating model (10 minute read)
item.description: An implementation guide breaks an OT security program into six components, beginning with asset discovery and process context mapping that tie every device to the operational process it supports. Availability and process safety outrank confidentiality here, so access boundaries, monitoring, incident response, and recovery each require joint sign-off from operations before deployment. Ownership belongs to a cross-functional executive such as a CISO or VP of Operations, with NERC CIP and NIST SP 800-82 treated as checkpoints rather than as the program design itself.

item.title: Are pentests obsolete in the AI era? (Sponsor)
item.description: You can now get the depth of a pentest at the frequency of a scan. Does that mean pentests are dead? This Intruder blog lays out the short-term, mid-term, and long-term implications of AI-driven pentesting. See what the economics, frontier AI developments, and threat landscape are all pointing to. Read the blog

item.title: Ditto (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Ditto is a tree-sitter-based PowerShell and JavaScript obfuscatory.

item.title: Natural Language Nmap (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Natural language nmap (nmap-nl) is a lightweight, local command-line inference tool that translates natural language into raw nmap commands and executes them locally using a locally-hosted, fine-tuned Gemma-3-270M model.

item.title: TATS (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Token Analysis and Tracking System (TATS) allows users to track OAuth 2.0, OIDC, and Microsoft Entra ID tokens across captured network traffic by ingesting Burp Suite XML exports, mitmproxy flow files, or live Chrome DevTools Protocol streams and serving an interactive web dashboard.

item.title: Our framework for reporting model misalignment (5 minute read)
item.description: OpenAI released a disclosure process and six incident reports. Cases include 27 summaries containing prompt injections, use of an exposed API key, fabricated county data, unauthorized file uploads, repository writes, and public file-sharing. Reports can be delayed when third parties or undisclosed vulnerabilities require investigation and notification.

item.title: Hackers Cracked a Flock Camera. Here Is What Was Inside. (3 minute read)
item.description: A removed Flock camera exposed 1.6 million images and records of 50,200 vehicles over 21 days. Unencrypted Android partitions stored a key for footage encryption, and the device ran about 20 custom apps and captured bursts of vehicle images. Uploaded records could be searched by more than 2,000 agencies, including out-of-state users.

item.title: Researchers used Claude to hack OpenAI (2 minute read)
item.description: Hacktron AI researchers used Anthropic's security tool to exploit an OpenAI community-forum configuration flaw. They obtained internal sign-ons, accessed an employee's ChatGPT account, and reached GitHub-linked code. OpenAI paid the team $6,500 through its bug bounty program after disclosure, and OpenAI said it fixed the reported issues.

item.title: Zero-click RCE vulnerability hit four major AI coding agents, two remain unpatched (3 minute read)
item.description: Plugin4Shell bypasses SHA pinning in Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, and Gemini CLI plugins.

item.title: International Meteor Organization says cyberattack dealt ‘critical blow' to website (1 minute read)
item.description: A cyberattack took much of the International Meteor Organization's aging web infrastructure offline.

item.title: Critical Pre-Auth RCE in Orkes Conductor Workflow Platform Exploited in the Wild (2 minute read)
item.description: Attackers are actively exploiting a critical pre-auth RCE (CVE-2026-58138) in Orkes Conductor by escaping unsandboxed GraalVM evaluators to execute arbitrary OS commands, requiring an immediate upgrade to version 3.30.2.

item.title: The EU AI Act: What Security Leaders Need to Know Now (Sponsor)
item.description: The EU AI Act is reshaping how organizations govern AI. Security leaders need clear visibility into where AI is used, the data it can access, and the controls they can demonstrate.Join us on Weds, Oct 7th to learn:→ The AI security implications of the EU AI Act→ The five AI governance gaps that leave security teams exposed→ Technical controls that can help support complianceCan't attend? Register anyways for the recording →

item.title: First Agentic AI Data Breach Reported to Spanish Regulator (2 minute read)
item.description: Spain's AEPD received a breach notification involving an automated system. It logged in, searched for flaws, changed personal data, and accessed invoices. Possible causes include a jailbroken model, an exposed test environment, or an unauthorized penetration-testing setup. The regulator calls for faster detection, containment, and response, plus stronger protection for digital identities and credentials.

item.title: Wordfence Argus Identifies Two Critical Unauthenticated Vulnerability Chains Leading to Remote Code Execution in The Events Calendar Plugin (6 minute read)
item.description: Two CVSS 9.8 flaws affect The Events Calendar up to version 6.17.4. Anonymous attackers can submit crafted Gutenberg markup in event comments and then trigger execution via pending-comment previews. One chain executes OS commands via PHP object injection, while the other resets an administrator password using wp_update_user. Update to 6.17.4.1. Exploitation requires comments enabled on event pages.

item.title: Hackers publish thousands of drivers' data after breaching Florida motor vehicle database (1 minute read)
item.description: ShinyHunters published hundreds of thousands of files stolen from Florida's DAVID vehicle and driver database after alleging the state agency refused to pay a ransom. FLHSMV confirmed that attackers used police credentials stored on a personal device. Leaked ownership records include names, addresses, buyer and seller details, and VINs. Some files also contain Social Security numbers, passports, and immigration documents.

item.title: Bring Your Own EDR: How to Turn a Commercial EDR into a Trojan Horse (10 minute read)
item.description: Researchers from Akamai discovered that attackers with admin access on a Windows device could abuse SentinelOne's EDR solution to dump protected processes, pivot to Microsoft Defender, and run malicious code in the Protected Process Light (PPL) context. They then extended this research by demonstrating how they could temporarily disable the EDR, move code into the EDR's protected files, run malicious code, and then re-enable the EDR, which would then protect the malicious code as part of its local files. Additionally, they found that cloud communication can be disabled by modifying the local DNS configuration.

item.title: How to Evaluate LLMs Before Production (12 minute read)
item.description: When evaluating an LLM-based system to reduce false positives in GitHub secrets scanning, the team faced issues that made benchmarks unrepresentative of production workloads and prevented them from properly evaluating model performance. To combat this problem, the team at GitHub created an LLM evaluation framework. First, teams should define the product decision that the system should support; then teams should make sure that offline experiments use a representative dataset and have only one clearly defined variable; error analysis and LLM-as-judge systems can be used to guide human analysts towards interesting aspects of the evaluation; and then finally the experiment can be promoted to production.

item.title: Agentic Self-Modification in Open-Weights Systems (9 minute read)
item.description: A coding agent fixed a failing query application by fine-tuning its shared Qwen model. It then merged the update into the default checkpoint, altering later agent and application instances, with held-out query accuracy rising from 0/20 to 20/20. The tuned model reproduced a synthetic API key, email, and address from training data and removed a trained refusal policy. Training tools, weight access, and deployment access increased modification attempts so as to track model lineage, retain training data and evaluations, and require approval before deployment.

item.title: Comp AI (Product Launch)
item.description: Comp AI provides software for governance, risk, and compliance work. It automates onboarding, evidence collection, policy drafting, control monitoring, and assessments.

item.title: neEDRe (GitHub Repo)
item.description: neEDRe is a toy EDR project that demonstrates how to implement an EDR system using AYA, the Rust eBPF library.

item.title: logtotal-sanitizer (GitHub Repo)
item.description: logtotal-sanitizer is a framework-agnostic log sanitizer for browsers and Node.js that is designed to sanitize log files before they are sent to third-party platforms for processing, analysis, or troubleshooting.

item.title: CISA Promotes a Fresh Way to Deter Cyberattackers: Lie to Them (2 minute read)
item.description: CISA has published its first-ever guidance on setting up honeypot systems, accounts, and data to distract potential attackers and ultimately help discover them. The guidance comes from internal discussions with CISA threat hunters and pentesters who found that cyber decoys can be a low-cost, high-fidelity way to detect attackers who have gained access to a network.

item.title: $1 Million Sandbox Challenge Uncovers Linux Kernel Flaws (3 minute read)
item.description: Vercel's two-week sandbox bounty received 1,285 reports and validated 92 findings, including one critical issue. No report accessed customer data. A leading submission chained two Linux networking flaws: one leaked host-kernel memory and another deterministically crashed the host. Patches remain under private review, and CVEs are pending.

item.title: Cisco Warns of Max Severity ISE Zero-Day Exploited in Attacks (2 minute read)
item.description: Cisco released security updates to address vulnerabilities in its Identity Services Engine, including a maximum-severity authentication bypass. An attacker could exploit the vulnerability to bypass authentication in the web-based management interface by sending a crafted request to affected endpoints. The Cisco PSIRT has identified this vulnerability as actively exploited and urges customers to update immediately.

item.title: Be alert: targeted attacks on prominent Rustaceans (1 minute read)
item.description: Prominent Rust maintainers are being lured onto fake job and contract video calls that end with a request to install a missing audio codec or paste a clipboard command.

item.title: Data Broker Radaris Loses Domains in Privacy Fight (4 minute read)
item.description: A New Jersey court transferred 14 Radaris-linked domains to Atlas Data Privacy after defendants missed court deadlines in Daniel's Law litigation.

item.title: Attackers Exploit Issabel Framework Flaw Enabling Unauthenticated OS Command Execution (1 minute read)
item.description: CVE-2026-89026 lets unauthenticated attackers forge JWT bearer tokens in Issabel Framework.

item.title: Chinese Hackers Exploit Critical Tencent Software Flaw for One-Click Code Execution (3 minute read)
item.description: China-linked UNC3569 used a single crafted link to gain system-level code execution through Sogou Input Method, Tencent's Chinese-language keyboard app used by hundreds of millions of Windows users, and deployed its GrayRabbit backdoor. Gen Threat Labs found that CVE-2026-51990 chained argument injection in the sgbiz protocol handler with a bundled Chromium 80 browser that was six years out of date, ran without a sandbox, and dropped same-origin protections. Tencent patched the injection bug in version 16.3.0.3498, but the outdated Chromium engine behind the chain remained unchanged as of September 10.

item.title: Texas Utility CenterPoint Energy Confirms Data Breach After Hacker Claims 7.49M Records Stolen (3 minute read)
item.description: CenterPoint Energy confirmed an attacker pulled customer data through an external-facing API on September 12. A hacker using the alias "4d722e4d656f77" claims 7.49 million records, including names, phone numbers, billing addresses, account numbers, payment status, and partial Social Security numbers. The attacker says the API lacked WAF protection, rate limiting, and JWT/auth tokens, and stopped only after a CAPTCHA was added.

item.title: Human Attacker Hits Machine-Speed Exploitation of Marimo RCE (2 minute read)
item.description: A human attacker exploited CVE-2026-39987 to achieve pre-authentication remote code execution and harvest cloud credentials from Marimo notebooks. The Sysdig Threat Research Team observed the operator pivot from the vulnerable terminal WebSocket endpoint to an SSH bastion host in eight seconds to access an AWS Secrets Manager SSH key without using large language models. Defenders must focus detection efforts on the shape of the attack chain rather than specific operator fingerprints, because prompt injection traps designed for AI agents failed to identify the human actor.

item.title: ParaShells: Parallels Desktop Turns Appliance Install Into a Root Shell (9 minute read)
item.description: CVE-2026-90894 lets a non-admin macOS user gain root through Parallels Desktop's appliance installer. JFrog tested Desktop 26.4.0 build 57513 on Apple Silicon. The root daemon exposes a world-writable Unix socket where an unsigned local process can authenticate through PrlSrv_LoginLocal. A quote in sVmParentPath injects tar's --use-compress-program option, and tar then launches an attacker script as root. Parallels released version 27.0.0 on September 1 to fix this issue.

item.title: Threat Hunting with JA4/JA4S (+ Practical KQL Queries) (5 minute read)
item.description: JA4 is a TLS fingerprint that shows how a client connects, not just where it connects to. Unlike JA3, part of it is readable, so hunters can see the TLS version, SNI, cipher count, and ALPN at a glance. The post includes KQL queries to pull these values from Entra ID sign-ins and Defender network logs, so teams can learn what normal looks like and spot clients that don't match.

item.title: The £3 WiFi Extender With a Backdoor in Every Unit (13 minute read)
item.description: A £3 Z05L WiFi extender uses an MT7620 chip and a four-megabyte Winbond flash. Its firmware starts Telnet on every boot with root password 198277tt@, and the web API accepts requests without session checks, so a mac parameter can reach system() without validation, allowing root command injection. Firmware updates verify CRC32 values only, allowing forged images, and the firewall leaves inbound services exposed on bridged networks as the config partition stores WiFi credentials in plaintext.

item.title: Reach security professionals reading TLDR (Sponsor)
item.description: If you're reading this ad, you know they work. TLDR subscribers make a deliberate choice to open their inbox every weekday. You reach security engineers, CISOs, and infosec leaders at the precise moment they're most receptive to new information shaping their work. Become a TLDR sponsor.

item.title: vol-rs (GitHub Repo)
item.description: vol-rs is a port of the Volatility 3 memory forensics framework from Python to Rust.

item.title: Entrust turns cryptographic inventory data into security action (3 minute read)
item.description: Entrust added Cryptographic Bill of Materials (CBOM) import and export to its Cryptographic Security Platform, so teams can map which systems depend on weak or noncompliant keys and certificates and fix the riskiest first. The update also brings Ansible-based certificate automation, composite algorithms for phased post-quantum migration, and SPIRE support for AI agent and workload identities. The platform now runs as a service or on-premises, which matters as DORA, NIS2, and the recent US Executive Order push for CBOM-based inventories.

item.title: Hackuity (Product Launch)
item.description: Hackuity consolidates vulnerability and asset data from 130+ security products and ranks flaws by severity, exploitability, asset criticality, threat activity, and business impact. Teams can assign and coordinate remediation across security, IT, cloud, and engineering.

item.title: Gottheimer Pushes Back On Third-Party Audits of Advanced AI (1 minute read)
item.description: A new AI regulatory framework, the FRONTIER Act, includes a provision that would require third parties to audit the safety of new frontier models. Rep. Josh Gottheimer pushed back and stated that frontier models should instead need to be submitted to the federal government for a short-clocked review cycle before release.

item.title: Active Exploitation Attempts Target WSO2 API Manager JWT Bypass With Forged Admin Tokens (2 minute read)
item.description: WSO2 API Manager CVE-2026-5430 is under active attack. Forged JWTs using unsupported signing algorithms can bypass authentication and grant administrator access in affected deployments, including API Manager 4.1.0–4.6.0, API Control Plane, Traffic Manager, and Universal Gateway. Captured tokens carried admin privileges, and attackers may access backend endpoints, credentials, consumer keys, application secrets, and internal services.

item.title: Reverse-Engineering Find My People to Stalk my ex a Friend, Cause I Can (21 minute read)
item.description: An in-depth guide to how the author decided to reverse-engineer Apple's Find My system to register a Linux device and (consensually) track a friend. The author first started by attempting to use the iCloud web API but quickly discovered that it didn't support Find My. After reversing and fuzzing the flow, the author was able to reproduce the process by: authenticating to Apple's private service, registering the Linux machine as an IDS client, receiving the existing Find My share key, and using it to fetch and decrypt the friend's latest location.

item.title: Oracle Patches 800+ Vulnerabilities in September 2026 Security Update (2 minute read)
item.description: Oracle's September 2026 patch update fixed over 800 vulnerabilities across 17 product families, including more than 100 critical flaws and over 240 exploitable remotely without authentication.

item.title: Cisco email security boxes can be rooted by... an email (2 minute read)
item.description: Attackers are exploiting CVE-2026-76461, a 9.8 flaw in Cisco Secure Email Gateway appliances.

item.title: A Peripheral Path to SYSTEM - Exploiting Logi Options+ for SYSTEM Shells (7 minute read)
item.description: Logi Options+, Logitech's widely used app for configuring its mice and keyboards, allowed any standard Windows user to reach SYSTEM because its privileged updater trusted only pipe connections from an agent process the user could inject. Researchers at AmberWolf used that access to override the {depot} path via the reinstall IPC endpoint, which directed a SYSTEM msiexec call to an unsigned MSI that skipped signature checks because the manifest set isSystem to true. The bug is tracked as CVE-2026-12518 and was patched on August 19, so admins should confirm that fleets run a newer build and alert on msiexec spawned by logioptionsplus_updater.exe from user-writable paths.

item.title: ClickFix attacks are tricking Mac and Windows users into hacking themselves (2 minute read)
item.description: Attackers hijacked HBO Max's Reddit advertising account and posted malicious ads. The ads led to fake HBO Max pages with CAPTCHA-style ClickFix prompts that made the victims copy commands into Windows Command Prompt, PowerShell, or macOS Terminal. The commands installed infostealers that targeted passwords, active sessions, and crypto wallets. Reddit paused the ads three days after a user flagged them, though how the account was taken over remains unknown.

item.title: Mass-Scanning Campaign Exploits Vite Flaw to Extract Cloud Credentials From Exposed Dev Servers (2 minute read)
item.description: Attackers scanned exposed Vite development servers in August and exploited CVE-2026-39364. Crafted query parameters bypassed server.fs.deny and returned protected files through /@fs/. Observed targets included .env files, AWS credentials, Azure profiles, Terraform state, database passwords, and /proc data with requests spoofing crawler user agents and forged forwarding headers.

item.title: Beltdown2: Escaping the Cursor CLI sandbox (7 minute read)
item.description: A malicious workspace can place a core.fsmonitor hook in .git/config. Cursor CLI ran internal Git commands outside its macOS Seatbelt sandbox. A read-only prompt triggered git ls-files, which executed the hook. The proof payload wrote to $HOME, while sandboxed shell commands could not. Anysphere acknowledged the report and shipped Cursor CLI 2026.08.04-aaa8809, and the fix injects GIT_CONFIG environment settings into every Git spawn, disabling core.fsmonitor, custom hooks, and repository attributes.

item.title: FulcrumSec - A look at their tradecraft (8 minute read)
item.description: FulcrumSec, a financially motivated data extortion gang behind breaches at Manchester Airports Group, Arup, and Novo Nordisk, told Lab539 it runs up to 250 servers scanning client-side JavaScript and fresh bugs like React2Shell, then bulk-tests harvested credentials before picking victims. From there, it chains pivots through GitHub repos, AWS, Azure, and Secrets Manager without touching an endpoint, with a single Arup PAT reportedly opening about 10,000 private repositories. Defenders should baseline normal identity behavior and flag tokens that suddenly clone thousands of repos or enumerate unrelated secrets from unfamiliar infrastructure, since this activity relies on valid credentials rather than malware.

item.title: Unmasking Cloud Identities: From Behavioral Clustering to Automated Detection (11 minute read)
item.description: Unit 42 clustered the CloudTrail activity of over 40,000 identities across 125 AWS environments and found they fall into consistent functional roles like console admins, CI/CD runners, backup agents, and security tools, regardless of naming or assigned IAM policies. That behavioral baseline matters because attackers masquerade behind benign labels and existing permission profiles, so a backup service suddenly running admin actions stands out even when its permissions allow it. The approach distills into a lightweight classifier that runs as standard SQL, letting teams tag identity roles at scale without a full ML pipeline.

item.title: Teleport's bug made open-source SSH safer for everyone (Sponsor)
item.description: Teleport's first critical bug in a decade traced back to Go's SSH library, which is used industry-wide. Instead of quietly patching, they funded an audit. 9 new vulnerabilities surfaced. They fixed them, thanked the auditor, and published the results – protecting everyone running Go-based SSH. Integrity matters. Read more →

item.title: OpenHunterAI (GitHub Repo)
item.description: OpenHunterAI is a local AI red-team workspace that runs attacker-style assessments against web apps, APIs, and LLM applications you own, combining browser inspection, recon, ZAP, and a Nuclei adapter under one scan plan. Its differentiator is scope control, with domain verification, deterministic plans, and human approval gates before any sensitive validation runs. It also ships as a skill for Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini CLI, so coding agents can prepare scoped assessments that wait for human reviewers to sign off.

item.title: RF-Swift (GitHub Repo)
item.description: A powerful multi-platform RF toolbox that deploys specialized radio, hardware, and other security tools in seconds on Linux, Windows, and macOS - supporting x86_64, ARM64 (Raspberry Pi and Apple Silicon), and RISC-V architectures without disrupting your primary OS.

item.title: AIUC (Product Launch)
item.description: AIUC audits and certifies deployed agents against its AIUC-1 standard. Its service runs roughly 5,000 tests covering jailbreaks, hallucinations, and data leaks. Customers receive a 100-page report, with humans validating final audit results.

item.title: Two DGX Sparks, 33 Local Models, One Question: Can Local AI Actually Red Team? (38 minute read)
item.description: Roei Sherman evaluated 33 local models on a two-node DGX Spark cluster for red teaming capabilities. The evaluation consisted of a security capability that tested whether the models can reason by testing them with a three-phase red team scenario, a red team benchmark to test the willingness and accuracy of model responses, and a coding benchmark consisting of Aider Polyglot plus two custom suites. Sherman found that MoE models consistently performed above their model class across all three benchmarks, with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (FP8) winning the security capability benchmark, Qwen3-Coder-Next (FP8) winning the coding benchmark, and more mixed results on the red team benchmark.

item.title: Mythic C2 Activity at Internet Scale (5 minute read)
item.description: Mythic, an open-source C2 framework that lets operators mix agents, transport profiles, and a shared web UI, is popular with red teams but has also turned up in real intrusions, according to new Censys research. Censys tracked 131 internet-exposed Mythic hosts, and 115 of them still carried the default O="Mythic" or O="Mythic C2" certificate. One cluster Censys flagged paired Mythic with custom Rust implants, Discord-based C2, and a domain disguised as Windows telemetry traffic.

item.title: Standing access is an open door for attackersan attacker's all-access pass (Sponsor)
item.description: 33% of developers using AI agents say their organization has experienced a breach tied to overprivileged non-human identitiesreport security incidents from overprivileged NHIs. Learn why traditional controls fail and how to close the gap.

item.title: Automated security review for plugin releases (2 minute read)
item.description: WordPress.org scans each plugin release during a six-hour cooldown before update distribution.

item.title: 240,000 Hit by Data Breach at Japan's Digital Agency (1 minute read)
item.description: Japan's Digital Agency found that attackers exploited a publicly disclosed VPN flaw.

item.title: macOS 27 Golden Gate, macOS Tahoe 26.7, and macOS Sequoia 15.8 fix 200+ vulnerabilities (2 minute read)
item.description: Apple patched more than 200 macOS vulnerabilities across Golden Gate 27, Tahoe 26.7, and Sequoia 15.8, including kernel code execution bugs in AVEVideoEncoder and UDF, as well as remote code execution paths via Bluetooth, CUPS, and WebDAV.
